charities.limitations: The current site identifies AI Now as a nonprofit 501(c)(3) and says it has operated independently since mid-2022; the historical NYU origin is not treated as its current sponsor. This scope covers current policy research and coalition work, not all academic work associated with its name. Its no-corporate-funding statement is self-reported, not an independent financial audit. Research visibility, policy access and narratives do not establish causal changes or endorse every policy position. No named software license was inspected and no open-source badge is assigned.
charities.falsifiableClaim: Does a specific AI Now policy strategy used by a public-interest coalition lead to a documented, implemented accountability measure that would plausibly not have occurred otherwise, rather than only a citation or meeting?
charities.evaluationScope: AI Now Institute’s current independent nonprofit policy research and coalition capacity, not a present NYU-sponsored programme, a software platform or all downstream policy changes.
charities.selectionStatement: Illustrative, scoped inclusion; no independent evaluator recommendation verified in this batch

tooling.summary: Public policy research, strategic analysis and coalition learning can help civil-society organizations engage with AI governance without each building a specialist research team.

checklistAlignment.rationale: Strategic narratives and coalition analysis address how concentrated AI power is framed and contested. This is partial editorial alignment, not a verified redistribution of power.

reviewMethod: AI-assisted source research and qualitative mechanism sketches; no independent human validation yet. Dataset update date does not refresh older profile or evaluator-status reviews.
